newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian truck strike drives metals trade to a halt.
newsitem.headline: Indian truck strike drives metals trade to a halt.

text.p: Trade in non-ferrous metals came to a virtual standstill during the week due to an indefinite strike by truck operators across India, dealers said on Wednesday.
"For the last five days there has been no trading because of the transport strike," said Bombay Metals Exchange president Sharad Parikh.
"There is a total standstill. Prices have also not moved much," Parikh told Reuters. "Once the transport strike is over the fluctuations will start."
India's striking truck owners kept more than two million vehicles off the road for the ninth day on Wednesday while they negotiated with the government to solve the crisis.
The strike was triggered by a planned five percent service tax on road transport and a sharp rise in insurance premiums.
Dealers said the movement of metals from ports to consuming centres had come to a halt.
Parikh said metal traders were not able to sell the material since buyers kept away due to the transport strike.
"Whatever semis they are manufacturing are being stocked. Their stock levels are going up but they are not recovering the money," Parikh said.
He said prices of aluminium, zinc and copper have been revised since April 1 but the effect was not known due to the truck strike.
In the week to Wednesday copper lost 50 rupees to a quintal while aluminium gained 25 rupees. The prices of zinc, lead, tin and nickel remained unchanged from the previous week.
